segments.text: Let's derive the formula every board exam asks for.
Two large parallel plates, each of area A, separated by a small gap d, with plus Q on one and minus Q on the other, giving surface charge density sigma equal to Q over A.
We assume d is tiny compared to the plate size, so the field between them is uniform and the fringing at the edges is negligible.

Step one, the field in the gap. A single charged sheet produces sigma over two epsilon zero on each side. Between the plates, the fields of the two oppositely charged sheets point the same way and add, giving sigma over epsilon zero.

They add inside for a clear physical reason: the plus Q sheet pushes a test charge away from itself, while the minus Q sheet pulls it toward itself. Both effects drive the field in exactly the same direction across the gap.
Outside the plates, those very same two contributions point in opposite directions and cancel exactly, which is why the field exists only in the gap and nowhere else.
Step two, the potential difference. For a uniform field, V equals E times d, giving Q d over epsilon zero A.
Step three, the capacitance itself. By definition C equals Q over V, and dividing gives epsilon zero A over d.

Notice what happened in that last step: Q cancelled out entirely, confirming exactly what we claimed earlier — capacitance depends only on geometry. Filling the gap with a dielectric simply replaces epsilon zero with K epsilon zero.
Chalo wo formula derive karte hain jo har board exam poochta hai।
Do bade parallel plates, har ek area A ka, ek chhote gap d se separated, ek par plus Q aur doosri par minus Q, jo surface charge density sigma equal to Q over A deta hai।
Hum assume karte hain ki d plate size ke comparison mein bahut chhota hai, isliye unke beech field uniform hai aur edges par fringing negligible hai।

Step one, gap mein field। Ek single charged sheet har side par sigma over two epsilon zero produce karti hai। Plates ke beech, dono oppositely charged sheets ke fields same direction mein point karte hain aur add hote hain, jo deta hai sigma over epsilon zero.

Wo andar ek clear physical reason se add hote hain: plus Q sheet test charge ko apne se door push karti hai, jabki minus Q sheet use apni taraf khinchti hai। Dono effects field ko gap ke across exactly same direction mein drive karte hain।
Plates ke bahar, wahi do contributions opposite directions mein point karte hain aur exactly cancel ho jaate hain, isliye field sirf gap mein exist karta hai aur kahin nahi।
Step two, potential difference। Uniform field ke liye, V equals E times d, jo deta hai Q d over epsilon zero A.
Step three, khud capacitance। By definition C equals Q over V, aur divide karne se milta hai epsilon zero A over d.

Us last step mein kya hua notice karo: Q poori tarah cancel ho gaya, jo exactly wahi confirm karta hai jo humne pehle claim kiya tha — capacitance sirf geometry par depend karta hai। Gap ko dielectric se fill karna simply epsilon zero ko K epsilon zero se replace kar deta hai।

sections.title: Deriving the energy stored in a capacitor

board_events.text: Derivation: energy stored in a capacitor
Charging a capacitor means ferrying charge from one plate to the other, and this gets harder as you go.
Each extra bit of charge must be pushed across a potential difference already built up by the charge that went before it.
That integral is where the factor of one half comes from — it is the average voltage across the whole charging process.
The energy lives in the field itself, not on the plates — a genuinely important physical conclusion.

segments.text: Where does that one half C V squared actually come from? Let's build it.
Charging a capacitor means ferrying charge from one plate across to the other. And crucially, this job gets harder as you go along.
Each extra bit of charge has to be pushed across a potential difference that the charge before it has already built up. The first bit is free; the last bit is expensive.
When the capacitor already holds charge q, its voltage is q over C. Moving a further small charge d q across that voltage costs work equal to q over C, times d q.
Integrating that from zero charge all the way up to Q gives one over C times Q squared over two, which is simply Q squared over two C.

That integral is exactly where the factor of one half comes from. It is nothing mysterious: it is the average voltage across the whole charging process, since voltage climbed linearly from zero to its final value.
This work is stored as electrostatic potential energy, and using Q equals C V lets you switch freely between all three equivalent forms.
Finally, divide the energy by the gap volume A d, substituting C equals epsilon zero A over d and V equals E d, and you get the energy density: one half epsilon zero E squared.
That result carries a genuinely important physical message: the energy lives in the field itself, spread through the gap, not on the plates at all.
Wo one half C V squared actually kahan se aata hai? Chalo use build karte hain।
Capacitor charge karne ka matlab hai charge ko ek plate se doosri tak ferry karna। Aur crucially, ye kaam aage badhne ke saath mushkil hota jaata hai।
Har extra charge ke bit ko us potential difference ke across push karna padta hai jo usse pehle ka charge already build kar chuka hai। Pehla bit free hai; aakhri bit mehenga hai।
Jab capacitor already charge q hold kar raha ho, uska voltage q over C hota hai। Ek aur chhota charge d q us voltage ke across move karne mein work lagta hai equal to q over C, times d q.
Use zero charge se poore Q tak integrate karne se milta hai one over C times Q squared over two, jo simply Q squared over two C hai।

Wo integral exactly wahan se aata hai jahan se one half ka factor aata hai। Ye kuch mysterious nahi hai: ye poore charging process ka average voltage hai, kyunki voltage zero se apni final value tak linearly chadha।
Ye work electrostatic potential energy ke roop mein store hota hai, aur Q equals C V use karke tum teenon equivalent forms ke beech freely switch kar sakte ho।
Finally, energy ko gap volume A d se divide karo, C equals epsilon zero A over d aur V equals E d substitute karke, aur tumhe energy density milti hai: one half epsilon zero E squared.
Us result mein ek genuinely important physical message hai: energy khud field mein rehti hai, gap mein failli hui, plates par bilkul nahi।

board_events.text: CBSE level: capacitance and charge on the plates
Given: plates of area two hundred square centimetres, separated by one point zero millimetres of air, connected to a fifty volt supply.
First convert to S I units: area becomes two times ten to the minus two square metres, separation one times ten to the minus three metres.
Notice the answer sits comfortably in picofarads — a reminder that the farad is an enormous unit in practice.
Both plates carry that same magnitude, one positive and one negative.

segments.text: A clean substitution problem to anchor the parallel plate formula.
We are given plates of area two hundred square centimetres, separated by one point zero millimetres of air, and connected to a fifty volt supply.
The first move is always unit conversion: area becomes two times ten to the minus two square metres, and the separation becomes one times ten to the minus three metres.
Substitute into C equals epsilon zero A over d: eight point eight five times ten to the minus twelve, times two times ten to the minus two, all over one times ten to the minus three.
That works out to one point seven seven times ten to the minus ten farads, which is one hundred seventy seven picofarads.
Notice the answer sits comfortably in picofarads. That is a standing reminder that the farad is an enormous unit in practice.
For part b, charge is simply capacitance times voltage, giving eight point eight five nanocoulombs on each plate.
Both plates carry that same magnitude of charge, one positive and one negative — that is what makes it a capacitor in the first place.
Ek clean substitution problem jo parallel plate formula ko anchor karta hai।
Humein diye gaye hain plates area two hundred square centimetres ka, one point zero millimetres air se separated, aur fifty volt supply se connected।
Pehla move hamesha unit conversion hota hai: area ban jaata hai two times ten to the minus two square metres, aur separation ban jaata hai one times ten to the minus three metres।
C equals epsilon zero A over d mein substitute karo: eight point eight five times ten to the minus twelve, times two times ten to the minus two, all over one times ten to the minus three.
Wo nikal ke aata hai one point seven seven times ten to the minus ten farads, jo one hundred seventy seven picofarads hai।
Notice karo answer comfortably picofarads mein baithta hai। Ye ek standing reminder hai ki practically farad ek enormous unit hai।
Part b ke liye, charge simply capacitance times voltage hota hai, jo har plate par deta hai eight point eight five nanocoulombs.
Dono plates same magnitude of charge carry karte hain, ek positive aur ek negative — yahi cheez use pehli jagah capacitor banati hai।

sections.title: NEET speed trap: dielectric with the battery disconnected

board_events.text: NEET speed trap: battery disconnected, then dielectric inserted
A five microfarad capacitor is charged to one hundred volts, then disconnected from the battery. A dielectric of constant K equal to four is slid in to fill the gap.
The trap springs the instant a student assumes the voltage stays at one hundred volts.
So the voltage fell from one hundred volts to twenty five volts — divided by K, exactly as the fork predicts.
Speed rule: disconnected means Q fixed, so voltage, field, and energy all divide by K.

segments.text: Here is the trap N E E T reuses essentially every single year.
A five microfarad capacitor is charged to one hundred volts, then disconnected from the battery. Only afterwards is a dielectric of constant K equal to four slid in to completely fill the gap.
The trap springs the instant a student assumes the voltage stays at one hundred volts. It does not. Apply the fork: battery disconnected means Q is king.
The charge is locked at five microfarads times one hundred volts, which is five hundred microcoulombs. That number will not change for the rest of this problem.
Capacitance jumps to K times C naught, which is twenty microfarads. With charge fixed, voltage must fall to Q over C, giving twenty five volts.
So the voltage fell from one hundred volts down to twenty five volts. Divided by K, exactly as the disconnected branch of the fork predicts.

For energy, use the Q-fixed form, Q squared over two C. The original energy was two point five times ten to the minus two joules; the new energy is that divided by four, or six point two five millijoules.
Speed rule for exam day: disconnected means Q is fixed, so voltage, field, and stored energy all divide by K. Three answers from one decision.
Yahan wo trap hai jo N E E T essentially har saal reuse karta hai।

Ek five microfarad capacitor ko one hundred volts tak charge kiya jaata hai, phir battery se disconnect kar diya jaata hai। Uske baad hi ek dielectric constant K equal to four wala slide karke gap ko poori tarah fill kiya jaata hai।
Wo trap usi pal spring karta hai jab koi student assume kar leta hai ki voltage one hundred volts par hi rahega। Wo nahi rehta। Fork apply karo: battery disconnected matlab Q is king.
Charge lock ho gaya five microfarads times one hundred volts par, jo five hundred microcoulombs hai। Ye number is problem ke baaki hisse mein nahi badlega।
Capacitance jump karke K times C naught ho jaata hai, jo twenty microfarads hai। Charge fixed hone ki wajah se, voltage ko Q over C tak girna padta hai, jo deta hai twenty five volts.
Toh voltage one hundred volts se girkar twenty five volts ho gaya। K se divided, exactly jaisa fork ka disconnected branch predict karta hai।

Energy ke liye, Q-fixed form use karo, Q squared over two C। Original energy thi two point five times ten to the minus two joules; nayi energy wo divided by four hai, ya six point two five millijoules.
Exam day ke liye speed rule: disconnected matlab Q fixed hai, isliye voltage, field, aur stored energy sab K se divide hote hain। Ek decision se teen answers।

sections.title: JEE Main: dielectric with the battery still connected

board_events.text: JEE Main: battery connected, dielectric inserted
A ten microfarad capacitor is connected to a two hundred volt battery and kept connected. A dielectric of constant K equal to five is then inserted, filling the gap.
Battery connected means V is king, clamped at two hundred volts; capacitance rises to fifty microfarads.
That extra charge physically flowed in from the battery — something that simply cannot happen in the disconnected case.
The battery actually does delta Q times V, or one point six joules of work — half stores, half dissipates.

segments.text: Now the other branch of the fork, with the battery deliberately left connected.
A ten microfarad capacitor is connected to a two hundred volt battery and deliberately kept connected. A dielectric of constant K equal to five is then inserted, completely filling the gap.
Battery connected means V is king, clamped firmly at two hundred volts. Meanwhile capacitance rises to K times C naught, which is fifty microfarads.
For part a, the charge before insertion is ten microfarads times two hundred volts, or two thousand microcoulombs; afterwards it is fifty microfarads times two hundred, or ten thousand microcoulombs.
For part b, the extra charge drawn from the battery is simply the difference, eight thousand microcoulombs, or eight millicoulombs.
That extra charge physically flowed in from the battery, which is something that simply cannot happen in the disconnected case, where the charge has nowhere to come from.
For part c, use the V-fixed form, one half C V squared. The energy rose from zero point two zero joules to one point zero joules, a change of plus zero point eight joules.

One subtlety worth noticing: the battery actually does delta Q times V, which is one point six joules of work. Half of that stores in the capacitor and half dissipates as heat — the recurring factor of two.
Ab fork ka doosra branch, jismein battery jaan boojh kar connected chhodi gayi hai।

Ek ten microfarad capacitor two hundred volt battery se connected hai aur jaan boojh kar connected rakha gaya hai। Phir ek dielectric constant K equal to five wala insert kiya jaata hai, poora gap fill karte hue।
Battery connected matlab V is king, firmly two hundred volts par clamped। Meanwhile capacitance rise karke K times C naught ho jaata hai, jo fifty microfarads hai।

Part a ke liye, insertion se pehle charge hai ten microfarads times two hundred volts, ya two thousand microcoulombs; baad mein wo fifty microfarads times two hundred hai, ya ten thousand microcoulombs.
Part b ke liye, battery se draw kiya gaya extra charge simply difference hai, eight thousand microcoulombs, ya eight millicoulombs.
Wo extra charge physically battery se flow karke aaya, jo disconnected case mein simply ho hi nahi sakta, jahan charge ke aane ki koi jagah hi nahi hai।
Part c ke liye, V-fixed form use karo, one half C V squared। Energy zero point two zero joules se badhkar one point zero joules ho gayi, ek change of plus zero point eight joules.

Ek subtlety notice karne layak: battery actually delta Q times V karti hai, jo one point six joules of work hai। Uska aadha capacitor mein store hota hai aur aadha heat ban kar dissipate ho jaata hai — wahi recurring factor of two.

segments.text: This one asks you to derive a formula first, then put numbers into your own result.
A parallel plate capacitor of plate area A and gap d is filled with two dielectric slabs stacked one above the other, each of thickness d over two, with constants K one and K two.
The key physical insight: the same charge Q, and therefore the same density sigma, sits on the plates and threads through both slabs in turn.
In a medium of constant K i, the field is sigma over K i epsilon zero, so the potential drop across a slab of thickness d over two is Q d over two K i epsilon zero A.
The total voltage across the capacitor is the sum of the two drops, which factors neatly into Q d over two epsilon zero A, times the quantity one over K one plus one over K two.
Dividing Q by that total voltage gives the capacitance: two epsilon zero A over d, times K one K two over K one plus K two.
Substituting area one times ten to the minus two square metres, gap four times ten to the minus three metres, K one equal to two and K two equal to four, gives about fifty nine picofarads.

Notice the deeper structure hiding in that result: stacked slabs share the charge and split the voltage, which means they behave exactly like two capacitors in series — even before we formally name that idea.

Ek parallel plate capacitor, plate area A aur gap d ka, do dielectric slabs se filled hai jo ek doosre ke upar stacked hain, har ek thickness d over two ki, constants K one aur K two ke saath।
Key physical insight: wahi charge Q, aur isliye wahi density sigma, plates par baithta hai aur baari baari dono slabs se thread karta hai।
Constant K i wale medium mein, field hota hai sigma over K i epsilon zero, isliye thickness d over two wale slab ke across potential drop hota hai Q d over two K i epsilon zero A.

sections.title: Pitfalls: the battery check and the right energy formula

board_events.text: Common pitfalls in capacitance and dielectrics
Believing capacitance depends on Q or V. It does not — only area, separation, and dielectric.
If a problem implies capacitance changed, the geometry or dielectric changed — never just the charge or voltage.
Skipping the battery check is the number one error in this whole subtopic.
Picking the wrong energy formula buries the K-scaling under unnecessary algebra.
Forgetting that energy scales with the square of voltage, and that charging always wastes half the battery's energy as heat.
Pro-tip: build a two-branch reflex. Disconnected? Write Q at the top of your page as a constant, then read off everything else.
Connected? Write V at the top as a constant, then charge and energy both scale as K, while field stays unchanged.

segments.text: Let's consolidate the traps this subtopic sets, one after another.
First: believing capacitance depends on Q or on V. It does not. Capacitance is fixed by area, separation, and dielectric, full stop.
So if a problem implies capacitance changed, look for a change in geometry or in the dielectric. Never accept a change in charge or voltage as the explanation.
Second, and this is the number one error in the whole subtopic: skipping the battery check. Disconnected means Q is fixed; connected means V is fixed. Decide it first, every single time.
Third: picking the wrong energy formula. Use Q squared over two C when Q is fixed, and one half C V squared when V is fixed. The right choice makes the K-scaling obvious; the wrong one buries it.
Fourth: forgetting that energy scales with the square of voltage, and that charging always wastes exactly half the battery's energy as heat, regardless of the resistance in the circuit.

<whisper> Pro-tip: build a two-branch reflex. If disconnected, write Q at the top of your page as a constant, then read off V equals Q over C, E equals V over d, and U equals Q squared over two C — all scaling as one over K.

If connected instead, write V at the top as your constant, then charge and energy both scale as K while the field stays unchanged. Two clean templates cover almost every dielectric question you will ever be asked.
Chalo ek ke baad ek is subtopic ke traps ko consolidate karte hain।
Pehla: ye maanna ki capacitance Q ya V par depend karta hai। Wo nahi karta। Capacitance area, separation, aur dielectric se fix hota hai, full stop।
Toh agar koi problem imply kare ki capacitance badla, to geometry ya dielectric mein change dhoondo। Charge ya voltage ke change ko explanation ke roop mein kabhi accept mat karo।
Doosra, aur ye poore subtopic ki number one error hai: battery check skip kar dena। Disconnected matlab Q fixed hai; connected matlab V fixed hai। Isse pehle decide karo, har single baar।

Teesra: galat energy formula pick karna। Q squared over two C use karo jab Q fixed ho, aur one half C V squared jab V fixed ho। Sahi choice K-scaling ko obvious bana deti hai; galat wali use dabaa deti hai।

Chautha: ye bhoolna ki energy voltage ke square ke saath scale karti hai, aur ki charging hamesha battery ki energy ka exactly half heat ke roop mein waste karti hai, circuit ke resistance se koi farak nahi padta।

<whisper> Pro-tip: ek two-branch reflex banao। Agar disconnected hai, to Q ko apne page ke top par constant likho, phir read off karo V equals Q over C, E equals V over d, aur U equals Q squared over two C — sab one over K ki tarah scale karte hue।

Agar connected hai instead, to V ko top par apna constant likho, phir charge aur energy dono K ki tarah scale karte hain jabki field unchanged rehta hai। Do clean templates almost har dielectric question cover kar lete hain jo tumse kabhi pooche jaayenge।

board_events.text: The moment an external field appears, the electrons shuffle until they set up their own field that exactly cancels the intruder.
The field inside the body of a conductor is not small — it is exactly zero, in equilibrium.
If it were not zero, the free charges would still feel a force and still be moving, contradicting the word equilibrium.
The crowd only settles once nobody is being pushed at all.
Every result in this subtopic holds only in electrostatic equilibrium — while current flows in a wire, the field inside is not zero.

segments.text: <curious> A conductor is a material packed with free electrons that can roam wherever the field pushes them. That single fact decides everything in this subtopic.
Think of those free electrons as an obedient crowd that instantly rearranges itself to kill any field trying to push it around.
The moment an external field appears, the electrons shuffle around until they have set up their own field that exactly cancels the intruder, everywhere inside the metal.
So the headline result is this: the field inside the body of a conductor is not merely small. It is exactly zero, in electrostatic equilibrium.
The argument is airtight: if that field were not zero, the free charges would still be feeling a force and would still be moving, which contradicts the very word equilibrium.
Put simply: the crowd only settles once nobody is being pushed at all. That settled state is exactly what we mean by equilibrium.

One important boundary: every result in this subtopic holds only in electrostatic equilibrium, with charges at rest. While charges are still flowing, as in a wire carrying current, the field inside is definitely not zero.
<curious> Conductor ek aisa material hai jo free electrons se bhara hua hai jo wahan roam kar sakte hain jahan field unhe push kare। Wo ek fact is poore subtopic mein sab kuch decide kar deta hai।
Un free electrons ko ek obedient crowd samjho jo turant apne aap ko rearrange kar leti hai kisi bhi field ko maarne ke liye jo use push karne ki koshish kar raha ho।
Jaise hi koi external field appear hota hai, electrons shuffle karte hain jab tak wo apna khud ka field set up na kar lein jo intruder ko exactly cancel kar de, metal ke andar har jagah।
Toh headline result ye hai: conductor ke body ke andar field sirf chhota nahi hai। Wo exactly zero hai, electrostatic equilibrium mein।
Argument airtight hai: agar wo field zero nahi hota, to free charges abhi bhi force feel kar rahe hote aur abhi bhi move kar rahe hote, jo khud equilibrium shabd ko contradict karta hai।
Simply kahein to: crowd tabhi settle hoti hai jab koi bhi push nahi ho raha ho। Wahi settled state exactly wo hai jise hum equilibrium kehte hain।

Ek important boundary: is subtopic ka har result sirf electrostatic equilibrium mein hold karta hai, charges at rest ke saath। Jab charges abhi bhi flow kar rahe hain, jaise current carry karti wire mein, tab andar field definitely zero nahi hota।

sections.title: Charge on the surface, and one big equipotential blob

board_events.text: All excess charge sits on the surface
Imagine any closed Gaussian surface drawn just inside the metal; the field on it is zero, so the flux through it is zero.
By Gauss's law, zero flux means it encloses no net charge — and you can shrink that surface anywhere you like.
The only place left for excess charge to live is the outer surface.
Second consequence: since the field is zero everywhere inside, there is no downhill anywhere within the metal.
Moving a charge from one interior point to another costs no work, so every point sits at the same potential.
The surface is at that same potential too — a charged conductor is one big equipotential blob.

segments.text: From that one idea, that the field inside is zero, a whole cascade of properties follows.
Imagine drawing any closed Gaussian surface entirely inside the metal. The field everywhere on it is zero, so the flux through it must be zero too.
By Gauss's law, zero flux means it encloses no net charge at all. And you can shrink or move that surface anywhere you like inside the conductor, always getting the same answer.
So the only place left for excess charge to live is the outer surface. Not spread through the volume, not at the centre — on the skin.
The second consequence follows just as directly. Since the field is zero everywhere inside, there is no downhill anywhere within the metal for a charge to roll along.
Moving a charge from one interior point to any other costs exactly zero work, which means every point sits at precisely the same potential.
And the surface sits at that same potential as well. A charged conductor is, in the end, one big equipotential blob.
Us ek idea se, ki andar field zero hai, properties ka poora cascade nikalta hai।
Socho ki tum koi bhi closed Gaussian surface poori tarah metal ke andar draw karte ho। Us par har jagah field zero hai, isliye uske through flux bhi zero hona chahiye।
Gauss ke law se, zero flux ka matlab hai wo koi net charge enclose nahi karta। Aur tum us surface ko conductor ke andar kahin bhi shrink ya move kar sakte ho, hamesha wahi answer milta hai।
Toh excess charge ke rehne ke liye ek hi jagah bachti hai: outer surface। Volume mein faili hui nahi, centre par nahi — skin par।
Doosra consequence utni hi directly nikalta hai। Kyunki andar har jagah field zero hai, metal ke andar kahin bhi koi downhill nahi hai jispar charge roll kar sake।
Ek interior point se doosre tak charge move karne mein exactly zero work lagta hai, jiska matlab har point exactly same potential par baithta hai।
Aur surface bhi usi same potential par baithti hai। Ek charged conductor, aakhir mein, ek bada equipotential blob hai।

board_events.text: The conductor's surface charges rearrange to cancel any external field throughout the cavity.
This is electrostatic shielding — the Faraday cage, why you are safe in a car during lightning, why electronics sit in metal boxes.
But shielding is one-way: it protects the inside from the outside, while a charge inside the cavity is still felt outside.

segments.text: Now let's look at what happens right at the surface, and then just outside it.
Any sideways, tangential component of field would drag the surface charges along the surface. But in equilibrium they have stopped moving, so that tangential part must be exactly zero.
So the field can only stick straight out, or straight in, and its strength is set by the local surface charge density: E equals sigma over epsilon zero.
Notice that this is exactly double the sigma over two epsilon zero of an isolated charged sheet. The reason is that a conductor's field is one-sided, with zero field on the metal side.
Now the most famous consequence of all. Carve a cavity inside a conductor, with no charge placed in it, and the field inside that cavity is zero, no matter how violent the field outside.
The conductor's surface charges rearrange themselves to cancel any external field throughout the entire cavity. A hollow conductor is a genuine fortress.
This is electrostatic shielding: the principle behind a Faraday cage, why you are safe inside a car during lightning, and why sensitive electronics sit inside metal boxes.
But note carefully the one-way nature of it. Shielding protects the inside from the outside. A charge placed inside the cavity still makes its presence felt outside.
Ab dekhte hain ki exactly surface par kya hota hai, aur phir uske bas bahar।

Field ka koi bhi sideways, tangential component surface charges ko surface ke along drag karta। Lekin equilibrium mein wo move karna band kar chuke hain, isliye wo tangential part exactly zero hona chahiye।
Isliye field sirf seedha bahar, ya seedha andar hi nikal sakta hai, aur uski strength local surface charge density se set hoti hai: E equals sigma over epsilon zero.
Notice karo ki ye exactly double hai isolated charged sheet ke sigma over two epsilon zero ka। Wajah ye hai ki conductor ka field one-sided hota hai, metal wali side par zero field ke saath।
Ab sabse famous consequence। Ek conductor ke andar cavity carve karo, usme koi charge rakhe bina, aur us cavity ke andar field zero hota hai, chahe bahar field kitna bhi violent ho।
Conductor ke surface charges apne aap ko rearrange kar lete hain kisi bhi external field ko poori cavity mein cancel karne ke liye। Ek hollow conductor ek genuine fortress hai।
Yahi electrostatic shielding hai: Faraday cage ke peeche ka principle, kyun tum lightning ke dauraan car ke andar safe ho, aur kyun sensitive electronics metal boxes ke andar rakhe jaate hain।
Lekin iski one-way nature ko dhyaan se note karo। Shielding andar ko bahar se protect karti hai। Cavity ke andar rakha gaya charge abhi bhi bahar apni presence feel karata hai।

sections.title: Formula toolkit: conductors in equilibrium

board_events.text: Formula toolkit: conductors in equilibrium

board_events.latex: q_{\text{interior}} = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; \text{all excess charge on the surface}

board_events.text: Sigma is the local surface charge density in coulombs per square metre, and E comes out in newtons per coulomb, the same as volts per metre.
One more caution: surface charge density is not uniform on an irregular conductor — it piles up at sharp points and edges.

segments.text: Let's collect the results for conductors in one place.
First and most fundamental: the field inside the material of a conductor, in equilibrium, is exactly zero.
Second: the net charge anywhere in the interior is zero, so all excess charge resides on the surface.
Third: just outside the surface, the field is sigma over epsilon zero, directed normal to the surface — compare that to an isolated sheet, which gives only half as much.
Here sigma is the local surface charge density in coulombs per square metre, and E comes out in newtons per coulomb, which is the same thing as volts per metre.
Fourth: the potential is constant throughout the conductor, interior and surface alike.
And fifth, for a cavity with a charge plus q enclosed in an otherwise neutral conductor: the inner surface carries minus q, and the outer surface carries plus q.

One more caution worth carrying: surface charge density is not uniform on an irregular conductor. It piles up wherever the surface is sharply curved, at points and edges, which is exactly why lightning rods are pointed.
Chalo conductors ke results ek jagah collect karte hain।
Pehla aur sabse fundamental: conductor ke material ke andar field, equilibrium mein, exactly zero hota hai।
Doosra: interior mein kahin bhi net charge zero hai, isliye saara excess charge surface par rehta hai।
Teesra: surface ke bas bahar, field sigma over epsilon zero hota hai, surface ke normal directed — isko isolated sheet se compare karo, jo sirf aadha deta hai।
Yahan sigma local surface charge density hai coulombs per square metre mein, aur E nikalta hai newtons per coulomb mein, jo volts per metre ke barabar hi cheez hai।
Chautha: potential poore conductor mein constant rehta hai, interior aur surface dono mein।
Aur paanchwa, ek cavity ke liye jismein plus q charge enclosed ho ek otherwise neutral conductor mein: inner surface minus q carry karti hai, aur outer surface plus q carry karti hai।

Ek aur caution carry karne layak: irregular conductor par surface charge density uniform nahi hoti। Wo wahan pile up hoti hai jahan surface sharply curved ho, points aur edges par, aur exactly isliye lightning rods pointed hote hain।

sections.title: Formula toolkit: spherical conductors and capacitors

board_events.text: Spherical conductors and the spherical capacitor
The field inside such a sphere is zero, while outside it is exactly as if all the charge sat at the centre.
Notice the b minus a in the denominator: a small gap gives a large capacitance, the same lesson as the parallel plate's one over d.
A useful rule for shell potentials: a shell contributes k q over its own radius at points inside or on it, and k q over r at points outside.
That single rule makes concentric-shell potential problems almost mechanical.

segments.text: Two geometries come up again and again in exam problems on conductors.
For an isolated spherical conductor of radius R carrying charge Q, the potential is one over four pi epsilon zero, times Q over R.
Dividing Q by that potential gives its capacitance: four pi epsilon zero times R. Once again, pure geometry — just the radius.
The field inside such a sphere is zero, as it must be for any conductor, while outside it behaves exactly as if all the charge were concentrated at the centre.
For a spherical capacitor, meaning two concentric shells of inner radius a and outer radius b, the capacitance is four pi epsilon zero times a b over b minus a.
Notice the b minus a sitting in the denominator. A small gap gives a large capacitance, which is exactly the same lesson as the parallel plate's dependence on one over d.
One rule worth memorising for shell problems: a shell contributes k q over its own radius, a constant, at all points inside or on it, and k q over r at points outside it.
That single rule makes concentric-shell potential problems almost mechanical, which we will see put to work shortly.
Do geometries conductors ke exam problems mein baar baar aati hain।
Radius R wale isolated spherical conductor ke liye jismein charge Q ho, potential hota hai one over four pi epsilon zero, times Q over R.
Q ko us potential se divide karne se uska capacitance milta hai: four pi epsilon zero times R। Ek baar phir, pure geometry — sirf radius।
Aise sphere ke andar field zero hota hai, jaisa kisi bhi conductor ke liye hona chahiye, jabki bahar wo exactly aise behave karta hai jaise saara charge centre par concentrated ho।
Spherical capacitor ke liye, matlab do concentric shells inner radius a aur outer radius b ke, capacitance hota hai four pi epsilon zero times a b over b minus a.
Denominator mein baithe b minus a ko notice karo। Chhota gap bada capacitance deta hai, jo exactly wahi lesson hai jo parallel plate ki one over d dependence ka tha।
Shell problems ke liye ek rule yaad karne layak: ek shell k q over apni radius contribute karti hai, ek constant, uske andar ya us par har point ke liye, aur k q over r uske bahar ke points ke liye।
Wo ek rule concentric-shell potential problems ko almost mechanical bana deta hai, jo hum jald hi kaam mein lagte dekhenge।

sections.title: Deriving that the field inside vanishes and charge goes to the surface

board_events.text: Derivation: field inside is zero, charge lies on the surface
Reasoning step one: suppose, for contradiction, that a non-zero field existed inside a conductor.
The free electrons would experience a force and accelerate — charges would keep moving, contradicting electrostatic equilibrium.
Reasoning step two: draw a Gaussian surface entirely inside the conductor, just beneath its outer skin.
Since this holds for any interior Gaussian surface you care to draw, no net charge sits anywhere in the bulk.
All of it resides on the surface — that is the only place Gauss's law leaves available.

segments.text: This derivation is pure reasoning — no integrals needed at all.
Reasoning step one. Suppose, for the sake of contradiction, that a non-zero field somehow existed inside a conductor.
The free electrons would immediately experience a force and accelerate. Charges would keep on moving, which flatly contradicts our starting assumption of electrostatic equilibrium.
So the electrons must redistribute precisely until their induced field cancels any internal field. Hence, in equilibrium, the field inside is exactly zero.
Reasoning step two. Draw a Gaussian surface entirely inside the conductor, just beneath its outer skin.
Everywhere on that surface the field is zero, so the flux is zero. By Gauss's law, the enclosed charge must therefore be zero as well.
And since this holds for any interior Gaussian surface you care to draw, however you shrink or shift it, no net charge sits anywhere in the bulk of the metal.
All of it resides on the surface. That is the only place Gauss's law leaves available, and it is why the result is so airtight.
Ye derivation pure reasoning hai — koi integrals ki bilkul zaroorat nahi।
Reasoning step one। Maan lo, contradiction ke liye, ki kisi tarah conductor ke andar ek non-zero field exist karta hai।
Free electrons turant ek force experience karte aur accelerate karte। Charges move karte rehte, jo humare electrostatic equilibrium wale starting assumption ko flatly contradict karta hai।
Isliye electrons ko precisely redistribute hona padta hai jab tak unka induced field kisi bhi internal field ko cancel na kar de। Isliye, equilibrium mein, andar field exactly zero hota hai।
Reasoning step two। Ek Gaussian surface poori tarah conductor ke andar draw karo, uski outer skin ke bas neeche।
Us surface par har jagah field zero hai, isliye flux zero hai। Gauss ke law se, enclosed charge bhi zero hona chahiye।
Aur kyunki ye kisi bhi interior Gaussian surface ke liye hold karta hai jo tum draw karna chaho, chahe use kaise bhi shrink ya shift karo, metal ke bulk mein kahin bhi net charge nahi baithta।
Saara ka saara surface par rehta hai। Wahi ek jagah hai jo Gauss ka law available chhodta hai, aur isiliye ye result itna airtight hai।

segments.text: This derivation explains one of the most-tested factors of two in the chapter.
Take a tiny cylindrical pillbox straddling the surface, with one flat face of area delta S just outside, and the other just inside the metal.
Inside the conductor the field is zero, so the inner face contributes no flux whatsoever. That face is completely dead.
Just outside, the field points perpendicular to the surface, as we established, so only the outer flat face contributes anything at all.
So the total flux through the whole pillbox is simply E times delta S — one face doing all the work.
The charge enclosed by the pillbox is sigma times delta S. Setting flux equal to enclosed charge over epsilon zero, the delta S cancels and leaves E equals sigma over epsilon zero.
Now the key question: why is this double the sheet value? For an isolated sheet, flux escapes through both faces, splitting evenly and giving sigma over two epsilon zero.
Here, the inside face is dead because the field there is zero, so all of the flux is forced out through one single face. That forcing is exactly what doubles the result.
Ye derivation is chapter ke sabse zyada tested factors of two mein se ek ko explain karta hai।
Ek tiny cylindrical pillbox lo jo surface ko straddle kare, ek flat face area delta S ka bas bahar, aur doosra bas metal ke andar।
Conductor ke andar field zero hai, isliye inner face bilkul koi flux contribute nahi karta। Wo face completely dead hai।
Bas bahar, field surface ke perpendicular point karta hai, jaisa humne establish kiya, isliye sirf outer flat face hi kuch contribute karta hai।
Toh poore pillbox ke through total flux simply E times delta S hai — ek hi face saara kaam kar raha hai।
Pillbox dwara enclosed charge sigma times delta S hai। Flux ko enclosed charge over epsilon zero ke equal set karne se, delta S cancel ho jaata hai aur bachta hai E equals sigma over epsilon zero.
Ab key question: ye sheet value se double kyun hai? Ek isolated sheet ke liye, flux dono faces se escape karta hai, evenly split hota hai aur sigma over two epsilon zero deta hai।
Yahan, inside face dead hai kyunki wahan field zero hai, isliye saara flux ek single face se bahar nikalne par majboor hai। Wahi forcing exactly result ko double kar deti hai।

sections.title: Deriving the capacitance of an isolated spherical conductor

board_events.text: Derivation: capacitance of an isolated sphere
A sphere of radius R carrying charge Q behaves, for all external points, exactly like a point charge sitting at its centre.
And since the whole conductor is one equipotential, that is the potential of the entire sphere, inside and out.
Capacitance depends only on the radius — pure geometry, exactly as always.
Notice how the Q cancelled again, just as it did in the parallel plate derivation — that cancellation is the signature of a geometric quantity.

segments.text: A short derivation, but one that reinforces the central lesson of the whole chapter.
Start from a fact we have already established: a sphere of radius R carrying charge Q behaves, for all external points, exactly like a point charge sitting at its centre.
So its surface potential, evaluated at r equal to R, is one over four pi epsilon zero, times Q over R.
And since the whole conductor is one equipotential, that is the potential of the entire sphere, interior included, not just its skin.
By the definition of capacitance, divide Q by that potential. The Q cancels completely, leaving four pi epsilon zero times R.
Look at what survived: capacitance depends only on the radius. Pure geometry, exactly as it was for the parallel plate, exactly as always.
Notice how the Q cancelled again, exactly as it did in the parallel plate derivation. That cancellation is the signature of a genuinely geometric quantity, appearing every time.
Ek chhoti derivation, lekin ek jo poore chapter ka central lesson reinforce karti hai।

Ek fact se shuru karo jo hum already establish kar chuke hain: radius R wala sphere jismein charge Q ho, saare external points ke liye exactly aise behave karta hai jaise ek point charge uske centre par baitha ho।
Toh uska surface potential, r equal to R par evaluate kiya gaya, hota hai one over four pi epsilon zero, times Q over R.
Aur kyunki poora conductor ek equipotential hai, wahi poore sphere ka potential hai, interior bhi included, sirf uski skin nahi।
Capacitance ki definition se, Q ko us potential se divide karo। Q completely cancel ho jaata hai, aur bachta hai four pi epsilon zero times R.
Dekho kya bacha: capacitance sirf radius par depend karta hai। Pure geometry, exactly jaise parallel plate ke liye tha, exactly jaise hamesha hota hai।
Notice karo kaise Q phir se cancel ho gaya, exactly jaise parallel plate derivation mein hua tha। Wo cancellation ek genuinely geometric quantity ka signature hai, har baar appear hota hua।

A solid conducting sphere of radius zero point one zero metres carries a charge of plus two microcoulombs.

segments.text: Three quick parts, each testing a different conductor property.
A solid conducting sphere of radius zero point one zero metres carries a charge of plus two microcoulombs. We want the potential, the field just outside, and the field at the centre.
For part a, potential is k Q over R, giving one point eight times ten to the fifth volts.
Remember that is the potential of the entire sphere, since a conductor is one equipotential. Not just of its surface, but of every point inside as well.
For part b, just outside the surface, the field is k Q over R squared, giving one point eight times ten to the sixth newtons per coulomb.
Equivalently, that exact same number is sigma over epsilon zero, computed from the local surface charge density. Both routes must agree, and they do.
And part c is free, if you have absorbed the core idea: inside the conductor, the field is exactly zero.
Notice something worth pausing on: at the centre, V is large while E is exactly zero. A live reminder that V and E answer completely different questions.
Teen quick parts, har ek alag conductor property test karta hua।
Ek solid conducting sphere, radius zero point one zero metres ka, plus two microcoulombs charge carry karta hai। Humein chahiye potential, bas bahar ka field, aur centre par field।
Part a ke liye, potential hai k Q over R, jo deta hai one point eight times ten to the fifth volts.
Yaad rakho ye poore sphere ka potential hai, kyunki conductor ek equipotential hai। Sirf uski surface ka nahi, balki har andar ke point ka bhi।
Part b ke liye, surface ke bas bahar, field hai k Q over R squared, jo deta hai one point eight times ten to the sixth newtons per coulomb.
Equivalently, wahi exact same number sigma over epsilon zero hai, local surface charge density se compute kiya gaya। Dono routes ko agree karna chahiye, aur wo karte hain।
Aur part c free hai, agar tumne core idea absorb kar liya hai: conductor ke andar, field exactly zero hota hai।

segments.text: N E E T reuses this cavity setup essentially every cycle.
A point charge of plus five nanocoulombs is placed at the centre of a cavity inside an electrically neutral conductor. We need the charges induced on the inner and outer surfaces.
Here is the trap: students forget that a neutral conductor must rearrange its own charge to keep the interior field zero. Neutral overall does not mean nothing happens.
Apply the cavity rule properly. Draw a Gaussian surface inside the metal, one that fully encloses the cavity. Since the field there is zero, it must enclose zero net charge.
The cavity holds plus five nanocoulombs, so for the enclosed total to come out zero, the inner surface must carry minus five nanocoulombs.
And since the conductor is neutral overall, whatever went to the inner surface must be balanced on the outer surface: plus five nanocoulombs.
From outside the conductor, the field looks exactly like that of a plus five nanocoulomb point charge sitting at the centre. All the inner detail is completely invisible from out there.
Speed rule to carry into the exam: an enclosed charge q gives inner surface minus q and outer surface plus q, for a neutral shell. Two answers in one line.

Plus five nanocoulombs ka point charge ek electrically neutral conductor ke andar cavity ke centre mein rakha gaya hai। Humein inner aur outer surfaces par induced charges chahiye।

Yahan trap hai: students bhool jaate hain ki ek neutral conductor ko apna khud ka charge rearrange karna padta hai interior field ko zero rakhne ke liye। Overall neutral hone ka matlab ye nahi ki kuch nahi hota।

Cavity mein plus five nanocoulombs hai, isliye enclosed total ko zero nikalne ke liye, inner surface ko minus five nanocoulombs carry karna padega।
Aur kyunki conductor overall neutral hai, jo bhi inner surface par gaya use outer surface par balance hona padega: plus five nanocoulombs.

sections.title: JEE Main: potentials of two concentric shells

board_events.text: JEE Main: two concentric conducting shells
An inner shell of radius zero point zero five metres carries plus two nanocoulombs, surrounded by a concentric shell of radius zero point one zero metres carrying plus four nanocoulombs.
The key principle: a conductor's potential is the sum of contributions from all charges, evaluated at its own radius.
For the inner shell, its own charge contributes k q over a, while the outer shell contributes the constant k Q over b everywhere within it.
So the inner shell sits at higher potential than the outer one: seven hundred twenty volts against five hundred forty.
The whole problem turns on one rule: a shell contributes k q over its own radius inside it, and k q over r outside it.

segments.text: This one tests whether you know the shell potential rule cold.
An inner conducting shell of radius zero point zero five metres carries plus two nanocoulombs. Surrounding it, a concentric shell of radius zero point one zero metres carries plus four nanocoulombs.
The key principle to apply: a conductor's potential is the sum of contributions from all charges present, each evaluated at that conductor's own radius.
For part a, the outer shell: both charges lie at or inside radius b, so each acts as if centred, and their total six nanocoulombs gives five hundred forty volts.

For part b, the inner shell, we need both contributions separately. Its own charge contributes k q over a, while the outer shell, being outside, contributes the constant k Q over b everywhere within it.
Adding those two: three hundred sixty volts from its own charge, plus three hundred sixty volts from the outer shell, giving seven hundred twenty volts.
So the inner shell sits at higher potential than the outer one: seven hundred twenty volts against five hundred forty volts.
The whole problem turns on one rule, worth memorising: a shell contributes k q over its own radius at points inside or on it, and k q over r at points outside it.
Ye test karta hai ki tumhe shell potential rule cold yaad hai ya nahi।

Ek inner conducting shell, radius zero point zero five metres ki, plus two nanocoulombs carry karti hai। Use ghere hue, ek concentric shell radius zero point one zero metres ki plus four nanocoulombs carry karti hai।
Apply karne wala key principle: ek conductor ka potential saare present charges ke contributions ka sum hai, har ek us conductor ki apni radius par evaluate kiya gaya।
Part a ke liye, outer shell: dono charges radius b par ya uske andar hain, isliye har ek aise act karta hai jaise centred ho, aur unka total six nanocoulombs deta hai five hundred forty volts.

Part b ke liye, inner shell, humein dono contributions alag alag chahiye। Uska apna charge k q over a contribute karta hai, jabki outer shell, bahar hone ki wajah se, uske andar har jagah constant k Q over b contribute karti hai।
Un dono ko add karke: apne charge se three hundred sixty volts, plus outer shell se three hundred sixty volts, jo deta hai seven hundred twenty volts.
Toh inner shell outer se higher potential par baithti hai: seven hundred twenty volts, five hundred forty ke against।
Poori problem ek rule par ghoomti hai, yaad karne layak: ek shell k q over apni radius contribute karti hai uske andar ya us par ke points par, aur k q over r uske bahar ke points par।

segments.text: Derive the formula from Gauss's law, then substitute numbers into your own result.
An inner sphere of radius zero point zero eight metres carries plus Q; a concentric outer shell of radius zero point one zero metres carries minus Q, with vacuum between them.
By Gauss's law, the field in the gap comes from the inner charge alone: one over four pi epsilon zero, times Q over r squared.
The outer shell contributes nothing at all to the field in the gap, because a Gaussian sphere drawn there simply does not enclose the outer charge.
Integrating that field from a out to b gives the potential difference: Q over four pi epsilon zero, times the quantity one over a minus one over b, which combines into b minus a over a b.
Dividing Q by that voltage gives the capacitance: four pi epsilon zero times a b over b minus a. The Q cancels once again, as it always must.
Substituting a equal to zero point zero eight and b equal to zero point one zero metres gives about four point four times ten to the minus eleven farads, or forty four picofarads.
Notice how that small gap, b minus a, produces a relatively large capacitance. It is the exact same lesson as the parallel plate's dependence on one over d, wearing different geometry.
Gauss ke law se formula derive karo, phir apne hi result mein numbers substitute karo।
Ek inner sphere radius zero point zero eight metres ki plus Q carry karti hai; ek concentric outer shell radius zero point one zero metres ki minus Q carry karti hai, unke beech vacuum ke saath।
Gauss ke law se, gap mein field sirf inner charge se aata hai: one over four pi epsilon zero, times Q over r squared.
Outer shell gap mein field mein bilkul kuch contribute nahi karti, kyunki wahan draw ki gayi Gaussian sphere outer charge ko enclose hi nahi karti।
Us field ko a se b tak integrate karne se potential difference milta hai: Q over four pi epsilon zero, times the quantity one over a minus one over b, jo combine hokar banta hai b minus a over a b.
Q ko us voltage se divide karne se capacitance milta hai: four pi epsilon zero times a b over b minus a. Q ek baar phir cancel ho jaata hai, jaisa hamesha hona chahiye।
A equal to zero point zero eight aur b equal to zero point one zero metres substitute karne se milta hai about four point four times ten to the minus eleven farads, ya forty four picofarads.
Notice karo kaise wo chhota gap, b minus a, ek relatively bada capacitance produce karta hai। Ye exactly wahi lesson hai jo parallel plate ki one over d dependence ka tha, alag geometry pehne hue।

sections.title: Pitfalls: sigma over epsilon zero, cavities, and one-way shielding

board_events.text: Common pitfalls in electrostatics of conductors
Using sigma over two epsilon zero for a conductor's surface field. That is the isolated-sheet result.
A conductor's surface gives sigma over epsilon zero, double it, because the field is zero on the metal side.
Thinking the field merely weakens inside a conductor. In equilibrium it is exactly zero, not merely reduced.
Forgetting induced charges on a cavity corrupts every field and potential value downstream.
Assuming shielding works both ways. A Faraday cage shields the inside from outside fields, but a charge inside is detectable outside.
Pro-tip: treat any charged conductor as a single equipotential and let Gauss's law do the heavy lifting.
For concentric shells, remember: a shell contributes k q over its own radius inside it, and k q over r outside it.

segments.text: Let's consolidate the traps this subtopic sets.
First: using sigma over two epsilon zero for a conductor's surface field. That is the isolated-sheet result, not the conductor result.
A conductor's surface gives sigma over epsilon zero, exactly double, because the field is zero on the metal side and all the flux is forced out one face.
Second: thinking the field merely weakens inside a conductor. In equilibrium it is exactly zero, not merely reduced, and the reasoning behind that is airtight.

Third: forgetting induced charges on a cavity. A charge plus q inside always induces minus q on the inner wall and, for a neutral conductor, plus q on the outer surface. Skip this and every downstream value is corrupted.
Fourth: assuming shielding works both ways. A Faraday cage shields the inside from outside fields, but a charge sitting inside the cavity is perfectly detectable from outside.

<whisper> Pro-tip: treat any charged conductor as a single equipotential, and let Gauss's law do the heavy lifting. To find interior charge, just draw a Gaussian surface there and read off enclosed equals zero.
And for concentric-shell potentials, hold on to that one rule: a shell contributes k q over its own radius at points inside or on it, a constant, and k q over r at points outside it.
Chalo is subtopic ke traps ko consolidate karte hain।
Pehla: conductor ke surface field ke liye sigma over two epsilon zero use karna। Wo isolated-sheet ka result hai, conductor ka nahi।
Conductor ki surface sigma over epsilon zero deti hai, exactly double, kyunki metal wali side par field zero hai aur saara flux ek face se bahar nikalne par majboor hai।
Doosra: ye sochna ki conductor ke andar field sirf weak ho jaata hai। Equilibrium mein wo exactly zero hota hai, sirf reduced nahi, aur uske peeche ki reasoning airtight hai।

Teesra: cavity par induced charges bhoolna। Andar ka plus q charge hamesha inner wall par minus q induce karta hai aur, neutral conductor ke liye, outer surface par plus q. Isse skip karo aur har downstream value corrupt ho jaati hai।
Chautha: ye assume karna ki shielding dono taraf kaam karti hai। Faraday cage andar ko bahar ke fields se shield karta hai, lekin cavity ke andar baitha charge bahar se perfectly detectable hai।

<whisper> Pro-tip: kisi bhi charged conductor ko ek single equipotential samjho, aur Gauss ke law ko heavy lifting karne do। Interior charge find karne ke liye, bas wahan ek Gaussian surface draw karo aur read off karo enclosed equals zero.

Aur concentric-shell potentials ke liye, us ek rule ko pakde raho: ek shell k q over apni radius contribute karti hai uske andar ya us par ke points par, ek constant, aur k q over r uske bahar ke points par।

Every capacitor in a series chain carries exactly the same charge Q.
The battery's voltage gets shared out across them, each taking a slice, and the slices add up to the total.
Each capacitor sees only a fraction of the voltage but holds the full charge, so the combination stores that charge at a higher total voltage.
Series capacitance is always smaller than the smallest member — like adding pipes end to end makes the flow harder.

segments.text: <curious> A single capacitor rarely gives exactly the capacitance a circuit needs, so capacitors get wired together. There are two basic ways, and they behave like opposites.
Connect capacitors end to end, so the same charging path runs through all of them. That is series.

Here is the key physical fact. When the battery pushes plus Q onto the first plate, that plate induces minus Q on the plate facing it. Since the inner plates are connected and isolated, that in turn pushes plus Q onto the next capacitor, and so on down the chain.
So every single capacitor in a series chain carries exactly the same charge Q. Not similar, not proportional — identical.
Meanwhile the battery's voltage gets shared out across them. Each capacitor takes a slice, and those slices add up to the total applied voltage.
Now think about what that means. Each capacitor sees only a fraction of the voltage but holds the full charge, so the combination as a whole stores that charge at a higher total voltage.
Higher voltage for the same charge means less capacitance overall. Series capacitance is always smaller than the smallest member, the way adding pipes end to end makes the flow harder, not easier.

<curious> Ek single capacitor shayad hi exactly wo capacitance deta hai jo circuit ko chahiye, isliye capacitors ko saath wire kiya jaata hai। Do basic tarike hain, aur wo opposites ki tarah behave karte hain।
Capacitors ko end to end connect karo, taaki wahi charging path un sabse hokar guzre। Wahi series hai।

Yahan key physical fact hai। Jab battery pehli plate par plus Q push karti hai, wo plate apne saamne wali plate par minus Q induce karti hai। Kyunki inner plates connected aur isolated hain, wo apni baari mein agle capacitor par plus Q push karta hai, aur aise hi chain mein aage।
Toh series chain ka har single capacitor exactly wahi charge Q carry karta hai। Similar nahi, proportional nahi — identical।
Meanwhile battery ka voltage un sab mein share ho jaata hai। Har capacitor ek slice leta hai, aur wo slices milkar total applied voltage banate hain।
Ab socho iska matlab kya hai। Har capacitor voltage ka sirf ek fraction dekhta hai lekin poora charge hold karta hai, isliye poora combination us charge ko higher total voltage par store karta hai।

Same charge ke liye higher voltage ka matlab overall kam capacitance। Series capacitance hamesha sabse chhote member se bhi chhota hota hai, jaise pipes ko end to end jodne se flow mushkil hota hai, aasan nahi।

segments.text: Now the opposite arrangement, and it behaves in exactly the mirror-image way.
Connect all the left plates together and all the right plates together, straight across the battery. That is parallel.
Now every capacitor sees the same voltage V, because they are all clipped to the very same two terminals. There is no way for them to see anything different.
Each one then grabs as much charge as its own capacitance allows, following Q equals C V individually, and all those charges add up to the battery's total.
Physically, more capacitors in parallel means more total plate area available to store charge. So the parallel capacitance is the simple sum of the individual values.
Here is the way to hold both arrangements in your head at once: spot which quantity is shared, and everything else follows automatically.

Series shares charge, so reciprocals add, exactly like resistors in parallel. Parallel shares voltage, so capacitances add directly, exactly like resistors in series. Capacitors are the mirror image of resistors — remember one and you get the other by flipping the words.
Ab opposite arrangement, aur ye exactly mirror-image tarike se behave karta hai।
Saari left plates ko saath connect karo aur saari right plates ko saath, seedha battery ke across। Wahi parallel hai।
Ab har capacitor same voltage V dekhta hai, kyunki wo sab exactly wahi do terminals se clipped hain। Unke kuch alag dekhne ka koi tarika hi nahi hai।
Phir har ek utna charge grab karta hai jitna uska apna capacitance allow kare, individually Q equals C V follow karte hue, aur wo saare charges milkar battery ka total banate hain।
Physically, parallel mein zyada capacitors ka matlab charge store karne ke liye zyada total plate area। Isliye parallel capacitance individual values ka simple sum hota hai।
Yahan dono arrangements ko ek saath dimaag mein rakhne ka tarika hai: pehchano kaunsi quantity share ho rahi hai, aur baaki sab apne aap follow karta hai।

Series charge share karta hai, isliye reciprocals add hote hain, exactly resistors in parallel ki tarah। Parallel voltage share karta hai, isliye capacitances directly add hote hain, exactly resistors in series ki tarah। Capacitors resistors ka mirror image hain — ek yaad rakho aur doosra shabd flip karke mil jaata hai।
